skill.name: npm-release
skill.description: Guide controlled releases of cc-devflow to npm, including version synchronization, changelog finalization, git tagging, publish checks, and recovery steps.
skill.summary: Guides cc-devflow npm releases with version parity, git tagging, dry-run checks, and registry verification.
skill.author: Dimon94

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms fixed path traversal references to sibling skill files and several high-impact release commands. Most command-substitution, reconnaissance, network, and entropy alerts are Markdown examples or normal release checks rather than malware. No prompt injection language was found.

remediation.suggestion: Vendor the DRY checklist into this skill or reference an audited packaged resource without ../ or ../../ paths.
Require explicit user confirmation immediately before git push, npm publish, npm unpublish, remote tag deletion, and revert steps.
Separate read-only checks from mutating commands and list preconditions for each mutating command.
Run the smoke test only for the expected package and version, and document that it executes package code.

content.value_statement: NPM releases fail when version files, changelogs, tags, and registry state drift. This skill guides a gated release with verification before and after publish.
actual_capabilities: Guides semver level selection for patch, minor, and major releases.
Checks release branch, clean worktree, version decision, and npm identity before publish.
Synchronizes package files, changelog entries, release commits, tags, and registry version.
Provides release commit and annotated tag message templates.
Runs dry-run publish checks and post-publish registry and help smoke checks.
Defines failure handling for push, publish, unpublish, tag deletion, and revert paths.
limitations: Targets the cc-devflow package flow; other packages need prompt adaptation.
Cannot validate npm credentials unless the agent has terminal access.
Does not replace human approval for real publish or unpublish actions.
Assumes Git, npm, and package scripts are installed and configured.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Maintainer Release
use_cases.description: Maintain a repeatable release path with clean branch checks, version parity, tags, and registry verification.

use_cases.title: Review Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Confirm changelog, package files, commit text, and tag text agree before publishing.

use_cases.title: Recover From Publish Failure
use_cases.description: Capture failed registry or push evidence and choose a controlled rollback or patch release path.

prompt_templates.title: Check Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a patch release for cc-devflow. Check branch, worktree, npm identity, changelog, and version files before any publish action.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Minor Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through a minor npm release. Create the release checklist, update changelog and package versions, and pause before real publish.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Parity
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit an existing release commit and tag for version parity. Verify changelog, package files, dry-run evidence, and smoke results.

prompt_templates.title: Recover Failed Publish
prompt_templates.prompt: Recover from a failed publish. Preserve commit and tag evidence, capture the registry error, and recommend the next safe release action.

output_examples.input: Prepare a patch release after two bug fixes.
output: A release plan with version level, branch state, changelog tasks, and required approvals.
A pause before any command that publishes or pushes remote tags.

output_examples.input: Check whether release version 2.5.0 is ready.
output: A parity report comparing package files, changelog, commit text, tag text, and registry state.
A list of blocking items that must be resolved before publish.

output_examples.input: The publish failed after the tag was created.
output: A recovery path that keeps local evidence, records the registry error, and avoids hiding partial release state.
A recommendation to retry, stop, or publish a corrective patch based on registry status.

best_practices: Confirm branch, clean worktree, and npm identity before changing release files.
Keep package files, changelog, release commit, tag, and registry version aligned.
Treat dry-run, publish, registry view, and install smoke results as required evidence.
anti_patterns: Publishing with uncommitted changes or unclear branch state.
Automatically switching branches to force a release target.
Deleting commits, tags, or logs to hide a failed publish.

faq.question: What package is this skill designed for?
faq.answer: It is designed for the cc-devflow npm package release workflow.

faq.question: Can it publish to npm automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide publish steps, but real publish actions should require explicit user approval.

faq.question: Does it handle version bumps?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides semver selection and package version updates before commit and tag creation.

faq.question: Does it verify the release after publishing?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires registry version checks and a post-publish help smoke test.

faq.question: Can I use it for another package?
faq.answer: Yes, but adapt package names, scripts, changelog rules, and registry checks first.

faq.question: What happens when publishing fails?
faq.answer: It keeps evidence, records the failure, and routes to retry, rollback, or a new patch release.
